children.value: Many recovery and learning problems combine smooth losses with constraints or penalties that are not differentiable. Solving them efficiently requires understanding both the cost of an iteration and the conditions for convergence. We begin with subgradient, projection, and barrier methods, then develop proximal maps and splitting algorithms, including ADMM and primal–dual schemes.
